alerts.summary: ### Impact `Schema.TemplateLiteral` compiles each `Schema.String` span to the lazy wildcard `[\s\S]*?` and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more `Schema.String` spans, for example: ```ts Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X") ``` the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. A 5,000-character string of `:` characters blocks the event loop for about 15 seconds. Applications that decode untrusted input with such a schema are affected. That includes `Schema.decodeUnknown`, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.is`, and anything built on them, such as `HttpApi` request payloads and `@effect/rpc` payloads. ### Patches Fixed in `effect@3.22.1` (#6

alerts.summary: ### Impact A bug in containerd's image manifest processing causes an unrecovered panic when a child descriptor contains the `io.containerd.manifest.subject` annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image through the transfer service (including default CRI `PullImage` requests) crashes the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes environments, `kubelet` retries failed image pulls with backoff, allowing a pod referencing an untrusted image to repeatedly crash containerd and disrupt container operations on the worker node. ### Patches This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.4.2, 2.3.7, and 2.2.10. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue. ### Workarounds Restrict pod image references to trusted registries (for example, using a Kubernetes `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` or admission webhook) and only pull or import images from trusted sources. ### Credits The con
